newsitem.title: CANADA: Onex buys IBM Canada unit Celestica, for $550 million.
newsitem.headline: Onex buys IBM Canada unit Celestica, for $550 million.

text.p: Canadian turnaround specialist Onex Corp. said on Tuesday it agreed to acquire electronics maker Celestica Inc. from IBM Canada in a C$750 million ($550 million) deal.

Onex President Gerald Schwartz said the company will consider launching an initial public offering for Celestica after expanding its presence in the fast growing original equipment manufacturing business around the world.
"This is an important acquisition for Onex," Schwartz told a news conference. "It represents a third leg in our company.

Schwartz said the purchase would help Onex establish more of a Canadian presence. He said while the company was based in Toronto it generated only about C$100 million ($73 million) from Canada out of revenues of more than C$8 billion ($5.84 billion).

It would be the largest acquisition to date for Onex, an investment company with interests in airline catering and auto parts. Last summer, Onex lost a C$2.3 billion ($1.7 billion) takeover bid for Canadian brewer John Labatt Ltd. to Belgium's Interbrew S.A.

Celestica employs about 1,000 people and produces computer memory boards and power systems. It manufactures computer parts for other companies under so-called outsourcing arrangements in Canada and internationally.
IBM Canada, a unit of International Business Machines Corp., spun off Celestica as a wholly owned unit in January 1994 as part of the company's worldwide efforts to revitalise operations.

IBM Canada President Khalil Barsoum said setting up the company as a separate entity helped Celestica attract more outside customers who would otherwise be reluctant to deal with IBM if they were also competitors.
He said it was the next logical step to sell off the company but maintained IBM would remain a significant customer of Celestica.
Celestica, one of Canada's largest exporters, has assets of more than C$600 million ($440 million) with annual revenues of C$3 billion ($2.2 billion).
It operates a 1 million square-foot manufacturing complex in Toronto and a design facility in Endicott, N.Y.

"It is our intention to substantially grow the non-IBM business while continuing to strengthen the relationship and develop further business with IBM," Onex Vice President Anthony Melman said in a statement.
Onex said it will invest at least C$100 million ($73 million) in equity in Celestica, making it the company's biggest shareholder and giving Onex voting control.
The companies said full details of the acquisition, which would include both debt and equity financings, would not be released until closing, expected in the next 60 days.
